data.cultural_impact: The name Satpal is deeply rooted in the rich cultural traditions of India and is considered a noble and revered name among Hindus. The emphasis on truth and purity reflects the Indianvalues of honesty, integrity, and moral character. This name carries a deep cultural significance as it represents the virtues that are highly valued and cherished in Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Satpal holds great spiritual significance as it symbolizes the inner journey towards truth, purity, and self-realization. It reminds us of the importance of being truthful in our thoughts, words, and actions, and of striving for inner purity and spiritual growth. Satpal is a reminder of the essence of our true self, which is pure, truthful, and divine. It inspires us to live in accordance with these virtues, leading to inner peace, happiness, and fulfillment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Satpal means 'Truth-Protector'. The name embodies the spiritual ideals of truth, protection, and righteousness. It is an auspicious name for one who strives to uphold truth and shield the innocent from harm.

historical_references.reference: Satpal Chauhan, a medieval Rajput ruler, is believed to have ruled the region of Mehron in present-day Pakistan between 1260 to 1290 CE. He is known to have expanded his kingdom and defended it against Muslim invaders, particularly the Mongols.

Another Satpal, a Hindu warrior and leader, is mentioned in the 15th century Sikh text, 'Guru Granth Sahib'. He is described as a brave warrior who was part of the army of Banda Bahadur, the founder of the Sikh kingdom in India, during the late 1600s.
historical_references.context: Hindu warrior and leader in the Sikh army
